GiottoClass

Source: AGENTS.md

The foundational S4 object framework for the Giotto Suite of spatial omics analysis tools. Defines the giotto object and all its subobjects, data access methods, the spatial manipulation verbs, and the generics that analysis packages attach methods to. Every other suite package (Giotto, GiottoVisuals, GiottoDisk) builds on the classes defined here.

  • Package version: 0.7.2
  • R requirement: >= 4.5.0
  • Primary spatial backend: terra (SpatVector / SpatRaster)

Search this file first; for deeper “why” follow the pointer to design.Rmd. If a decision looks arbitrary and you are tempted to undo it, check adr/ before doing so — the alternatives were often already tried. Write a new ADR when you make a call a future reader could reasonably reverse; format, criteria and numbering are in adr/README.md. Class Hierarchy

Two tiers: the giotto container (24 slots, mostly nullOrList) holds nested lists of subobjects. Subobjects are self-describing — they carry their own schema tags and are the unit that spatial verbs dispatch on.

Subobjects inherit from two independent families of virtual class at once:

# schema tags carried
provData        @provenance
featData        @feat_type
spatData        @spat_unit                    (contains provData)
spatFeatData    both axes                     (contains spatData, featData, provData)
nameData        @name

# how the payload is stored
gdtData         data.table-backed; [ $ nrow colnames behave like data.table
├── coordDataDT → spatLocsObj
└── metaData    → cellMetaObj, featMetaObj
exprData        → exprObj                      (matrix, Matrix, or a dataStore handle)
terraVectData   → giottoPolygon, giottoPoints  (external pointer)

# domain-specific
enrData → spatEnrObj    nnData → nnNetObj    spatNetData → spatialNetworkObj
spatGridData → spatialGridObj                miscData → has @misc

So spatEnrObj is nameData + enrData + spatFeatData + gdtData, and each contributes a different set of inherited methods. When adding a subobject, pick one virtual from each of the first two families, then a domain virtual only if there is domain-specific behaviour to hang on it. Rationale and the alternatives considered: design.Rmd, Subobject class hierarchy.

giotto slot lists nest to exactly the depth of the keys they need — no placeholder levels:

gobject@expression$cell$rna$raw     # spat_unit / feat_type / name
gobject@spatial_locs$cell$raw       # spat_unit / name
gobject@cell_metadata$cell$rna      # spat_unit / feat_type

Key constraints

initialize() runs on every set

The giotto initialize() method updates subobjects for class changes, ensures instructions, validates active spat_unit/feat_type, derives @cell_ID / @feat_ID, and runs hierarchical consistency checks. It is on the hot path of every setter. Loops that set many objects should pass initialize = FALSE where a setter exposes it and re-initialize once at the end.

ID derivation prefers @expression over @spatial_info/@feat_info. That ordering is what lets an object be built in either order.

@source is NULL or a backend manager

is.null(gobject@source) is the one test for “is this object backed” (ADR 0001). There is no null-object standing in for in-memory, so every write-through site guards explicitly.

On a backed object, set*() writes the payload to the vault via GiottoDisk::sourceWrite() and stores the resulting dataStore in the slot (ADR 0002). Two consequences for any code you write:

  • Setters perform I/O. They can be slow and they can fail.
  • A slot may hold a store rather than a matrix. Anything reaching for dim(), is.matrix(), or row/column names on slot contents needs a store branch. Validators (.evaluate_*()) pass store classes through unchanged — a validator must never materialize its input.

@h5_file is deprecated, kept in the class definition for one release so older serialized objects load. Do not build on it; do not remove it yet.

terra pointers do not serialize

giottoPolygon / giottoPoints hold a SpatVector — an external pointer to C++ memory. It does not survive saveRDS() or a trip to a parallel worker, and it fails silently: the object comes back empty rather than erroring.

Use saveGiotto() / loadGiotto() — serialization by reference. Each SpatVector is written as its own shapefile (.save_external(), plus a _names.txt sidecar since shapefiles truncate column names); the gobject is saveRDS’d separately with dead pointers, and .load_external() re-reads the shapefiles on load. Peak memory stays at one layer and the artifacts are independently readable.

wrap() / vect() and the packed* classes are unmaintained and may be removed — do not build on them (ADR 0005). Serialization by value copies every layer into the R heap, which does not hold at project scale. They remain only because GiottoData’s giottoPoints / giottoPolygon minis and older user .RDS files are stored as packedGiotto* and still have to read back. There is no runtime deprecation warning: the read direction is exactly the path that legitimately still runs, and deprecate_soft() could not separate it from a direct user call.

A new class wrapping a terra object gets .save_external() / .load_external() methods and no packed* variant. reconnect() is the raster equivalent — SpatRaster holds a file handle, written via writeRaster() and re-opened from the recorded path.

Networks store a graph in @network

Both spatialNetworkObj and nnNetObj store an igraph (or a GiottoDisk dataStore) in a slot named network (ADR 0004). Construction goes through createNetwork(x, param); the four legacy constructors are wrappers.

Known gap: accessors that reach into @network assuming igraph — spatIDs() on network objects among them — still need a dataStore branch.

Object versioning

@versions records the producing GiottoClass version; updateGiottoObject() is a linear sequence of version-gated migrations. Removed slots stay reachable via attr(gobject, "old_slot") because S4 deserialization keeps the stored representation — that is the mechanism for retiring a slot without breaking old files (.update_network_slots() is the worked example).

When you change a class definition, add the migration in the same commit.

Adding to the package

A new generic

Almost always the wrong move. Five analysis generics exist and are split by return contract (ADR 0003), and they are distinct, not synonyms:

generic returns
processData() same-shape transform
filterData() a selection (IDs to keep)
reduceData() a decomposition / embedding
clusterData() cluster assignments (param takes bluster::BlusterParam)
analyzeData() computed outputs and summary statistics

A new algorithm is a new Param subclass plus a method in Giotto or GiottoDisk — not a new generic here. Route to the generic whose return contract matches, or fall through to the ANY,ANY catch-all. A method attached to the wrong generic silently never dispatches.

GiottoClass defines these generics and the virtual Param classes and exports no methods for them.

If a generic genuinely is new, it goes in R/generics.R with an @rdname tag and no implementation.

A new class

  1. setClass() in the appropriate R/classes-*.R file.
  2. Export via @exportClass.
  3. Constructor (e.g. createGiottoFoo()) in R/create.R.
  4. Generics to R/generics.R; methods to R/methods-<topic>.R.
  5. If it goes in a giotto slot, update the slot type union in R/classes.R and R/zzz.R.
  6. packed* variant if it wraps a terra object.
  7. Tests in tests/testthat/.

A new method

Implementation goes in R/methods-<topic>.R, never next to the generic. A generic defined next to one of its methods reads as belonging to that method, and the next person adds a second generic instead of a second method.

Dispatch outside S4

R/flex_functions.R holds *_flex helpers (mean_flex, colSums_flex, …). They route to a method that is not the one defined for a class in its native package — usually to stop sparse Matrix operations from densifying — without polluting the user’s environment with S4 dispatch they did not ask for. Use the flex function as a drop-in replacement inside suite code, and prefer adding one over a bare setMethod on a base generic for a class this package does not own.

Coding Conventions

Full style guide: https://giottosuite.com/articles/coding_style.html Dispatch functions: https://giottosuite.com/articles/dispatch_functions.html

Naming

Type Convention Example
Exported user-facing functions camelCase createGiottoObject()
S4 classes camelCase giottoLargeImage
Exported utility / non-user-facing snake_case dt_to_matrix()
Internal functions .snake_case (leading dot) .detect_in_dir()
Parameters / arguments snake_case spat_unit, feat_type

Do not use periods as name separators — this conflicts with S3 dispatch. Do not use non-UTF-8 characters; use Unicode escapes instead (e.g. \u00F6).

Other

  • Style: 4-space indentation, BioConductor conventions (biocthis + styler). Enforced by lintr in CI.
  • Imports: all @importFrom declarations go in R/package_imports.R, not scattered across files.
  • Error handling: bare stop(..., call. = FALSE) with a [site] prefix naming where the failure came from, e.g. stop("[setGiotto] this space has no name", call. = FALSE). Not gstop() — it prepends the calling function automatically, which duplicates the prefix and reads worse from a deep internal frame. gwarn() / gmessage() are still the right thing for warnings and messages.
  • Validation: checkmate at function boundaries.
  • Data tables: prefer data.table idioms over base R for tabular work.
  • Never edit NAMESPACE or man/ directly. Run devtools::document() after changing any @export, @importFrom, or @param tag.

Development Workflow

devtools::load_all()     # Load package for interactive development
devtools::document()     # Regenerate NAMESPACE + man/ from roxygen2
devtools::test()         # Run testthat suite
devtools::check()        # Full R CMD check

Testing

devtools::test()
testthat::test_file("tests/testthat/test_03_accessors.R")

Test data comes from the GiottoData package via GiottoData::loadGiottoMini() and GiottoData::loadSubObjectMini(). Global setup is tests/testthat/setup.R:

options("giotto.use_conda" = FALSE)      # No conda during tests
options("giotto.no_python_warn" = TRUE)  # Suppress Python warnings
options("lifecycle_verbosity" = "quiet")

Numbered tests (test_01_*.R … test_10_*.R) run foundational object creation in order; the rest are named by functional area.

Dependencies

Imports (always required): terra, data.table, Matrix, igraph, dbscan, deldir, checkmate, matrixStats, reticulate, GiottoUtils

Suggests (optional): Seurat/SeuratObject, SingleCellExperiment, SpatialExperiment, sf, sp, stars, magick, HDF5Array, qs, and others — see DESCRIPTION.

Adding a dependency:

  • Hard requirement → Imports: in DESCRIPTION + @importFrom in R/package_imports.R.
  • Optional → Suggests: + guard usage with package_check("pkg", repository = "CRAN") (or "Bioc" / "github").

Branches and CI/CD

Branch Workflow Checks
staging staging_branch_workflow.yml R CMD check (macOS/Windows/Linux), codecov, BiocCheck
dev dev_branch_workflow.yml codecov, R CMD check, BiocCheck, lintr
feature branches feature_branch_workflow.yml codecov, R CMD check, BiocCheck, lintr

PRs target dev; releases are cut from staging → main. Exception: disk-backed / on-disk work targets gsource, the long-running integration branch where that arc is staged before it flows into dev.

BiocCheck runs to ensure Bioconductor submission compatibility.

Interoperability

Conversions live in R/interoperability.R. All are lossy — the schema above has no counterpart in most of these formats, so a round trip does not preserve provenance or multi-unit nesting.

From / To Function
Seurat v4/v5 → Giotto seuratToGiotto(), seuratToGiottoV4(), seuratToGiottoV5()
Giotto → Seurat giottoToSeurat(), giottoToSeuratV5()
AnnData → Giotto anndataToGiotto()
Giotto → AnnData giottoToAnnData()
SpatialExperiment ↔︎ Giotto spatialExperimentToGiotto(), giottoToSpatialExperiment()
SpatialData → Giotto spatialdataToGiotto()
